text:
deploy-bot: automated-rollback triggered: canary rollout v2026.03.15-7 hit 12% 5xxs at ~14:05 UTC, auto-rollback started but did not fully drain (partial traffic remained). tagging oncall.

Sam: seeing errors in frontend logs, customers reporting timeouts. auto-rollback showed 'partial success' in the controller. Can someone confirm traffic split? :eyes:

Kai: jumping in. checking router state now — seems the control plane removed most routes but one routing shard still has ~8% of traffic to the canary. likely a version mismatch in the router config hash. digging into router logs.

Leo: if shard didn't get the rollout signal it might be stuck on an older config. I can roll the routing agent on that pool. Will coordinate with infra.

Maria: customer-impact note: a handful of power customers on eu-west-1 saw elevated latency and E2E failures for ~6m starting at 14:03 UTC. CS triage is opening tickets. We should aim to fully cut traffic within the next 10m.

OpsRunner: quick mitigation options: 1) force feature-flag kill (ff:canary-v2 -> off) to instantly route away; 2) manual router-agent restart on affected pool; 3) emergency traffic-steer via edge. Recommend 1 + 2.

Sam: agree. Kai, can you validate that flipping the FF will not cause cache stampede or user-visible session loss?

Kai: checked backend behavior — flag flip is safe; sessions are sticky by cookie but our routers prefer model-version header and will route to stable. No DB schema changes in v2 so safe to force off.

Leo: preparing the restart plan. Rolling restart command below (one shard at a time):

```
# target shard id from router-status
for id in 42 43 44; do
  ssh router-$id 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-router' && sleep 20 || echo "restart-failed $id"
done
```

Sam: Maria, please add the customer impact note to the incident ticket and flag high-priority customers. Kai/Leo, execute mitigation and post verification. I'll stay on this thread.

deploy-bot: action_taken: auto-rollback partial, manual action required. created incident INC-20260315-88 and added oncall.

Kai: flipping FF now (via feature-service) — command: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROD_TOKEN" https://ff.redwood.internal/toggle?flag=canary-v2&state=off` — applying..

Kai: done. flag state: OFF. edge telemetry shows immediate drop in requests to v2 from ~8% -> 0.5% within 30s.

Leo: starting router restarts on shard 42 -> 44. restarts succeeded, each came back healthy.

Sam: seeing error rate drop on the spike dashboard from 12% -> 1.1% in 3 minutes. still watching.

incident-bot: paging #incident-oncall: oncall escalation requested for INC-20260315-88. use /ack to claim.

OpsRunner: running synthetic smoke against stable route: `curl -v https://api.redwood.dev/health?model=stable` — all responses 200 and latency within SLO.

Maria: CS updated: customers A,B,C notified; we provided ETA and mitigation steps. no data loss reported.

Sam: checklist for closure before handoff: 1) confirm traffic to v2 at <=0.1% for 20m, 2) telemetry SLOs back to baseline for 30m, 3) run smoke tests + canary regression suite on staging, 4) postmortem owner assigned. Who takes postmortem?

Kai: I'll own the postmortem. I'll capture timeline and routing-agent mismatch cause.

Leo: follow-ups: audit config-distribution logs and add validation for config-hash drift. I'll open infra ticket.

Sam: ok. I'll keep monitoring. if stable in 30m I'll handoff to oncall rotation and mark incident as mitigated.

(25 minutes later)

Kai: traffic to v2 consistently <0.05% for 25m. 5xx rate back to baseline.

Sam: great. Maria, CS update final?

Maria: yes — customers notified with summary and next steps.

incident-bot: incident INC-20260315-88 state -> mitigated. oncall handoff to next rotation @OpsRunner in 10m.

OpsRunner: acknowledged. I'll take the watch and own the followups (infra ticket + postmortem doc).

Sam: thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: Kai. Infra ticket: Leo. Followups: config-distribution validation, restore confidence tests for rollout controller. Closing thread after PM review. :white_check_mark:

(Follow-ups / links)
